caption: Day 1. Alda Reed sees the birth-flower.
prompt: FULL-PAGE COLOUR INSERT ILLUSTRATION for a light novel, portrait orientation, edge-to-edge composition with a strong focal point and cinematic depth; opaque, fully painted background. A cramped two-room birth room in a poor clay quarter, night, the only light a banked hearth glowing red under ash and one tallow candle. The trodden-ash floor; along the bottom of the clay-daubed wall runs a thumb-wide GREY RIDGE OF ASH that nobody sweeps. The plank door does not shut: frost and blue moonlight come through the gap. CENTRE: the midwife ALDA REED (see reference: grey shawl, linen cap, stooped, calm) lifts a two-hour-old newborn from a fold of grey wool and stares at a delicate BRANCHING RED MARK running across his tiny ribs and down one forearm like a frost-flower; two fingers of her free hand are crossed in an unconscious warding sign. On the bench at her elbow: a flat grey writing slate with chalk scribbles (no legible text) and a small milk-white river stone in a rag, its warmth visibly fading (faint heat shimmer). BACKGROUND, on a straw pallet, the exhausted young mother DESSA SILT (see reference) lies facing the wall, thumb pressing a pale scar on her forearm. The newborn's eyes are open and unnervingly focused, an adult mind behind them. In the hearth smoke rising toward the rafters, a faint ghostly double-exposure: an overturned van burning on a snowy modern highway under orange streetlights.
